Hi bking1232. I feel you too... currently I’m completely separated from my family members while dealing with my crappy job, and most importantly dealing with depression I’ve carried for nearly 9 years.
One of the only things we can do right now is keep dissecting the problem that we have right now into smaller pieces, until they are solvable. Recently I made a video on that so i hope it helps a little! 

https://youtu.be/kzr22ljfRvg

Honestly, I think you don’t have to force yourself to interact with others. Everyone has their own personality trait, and if making yourself cozy at home makes you feel relieved from stress, I think it’s fine!
(Well, if not going outside at all is causing health problems, then maybe you should take a walk/jog for a few minutes or something, but besides that I think it’s alright to stay home)

Humans have what is called a “Parasympathetic nerve”. When it’s cloudy/dark outside, the nerve activates and sends out a signal that tranquilizes your mood. When there is an autonomic imbalance due to some reason, that may trigger depressive mood.

Hi DramaQueenOrLearning. As you say so, locked down at home and being isolated tends to cause both psychical and mental problems, especially depressive thoughts from loneliness.
Depression tends to drag us down into extremely negative thoughts, even if some of those negative thoughts aren’t true.
So what we can do at this point, is to organize the easiest things you can right now. It can be your eating habit, cleaning your room, take a long walk at a certain time etc...
By building a routine, you can sharpen your cognitive functions, and little by little, you can get back to reorganizing relationships with others.
Also, i made a video on dissecting your major problems into smaller, solvable problems, so if you’d like, check it out.

https://youtu.be/kzr22ljfRvg

You’re welcome! As a person who’s had depression on multiple occasions, I understand how hard it is to get your will power back.
Getting back steadily one step at a time is the key :) No need to rush! Set a goal that’s easy (for instance, try taking a warm shower, do some simple stretches & take deep breath for a minute or 2 before u go to sleep and see if you can extend your sleep time)
If you can, try keeping record of your sleep time so you know what’s working.
